Finding 1: The AI Bottleneck Has Moved From Technology To Deployment

Rough summary:
Finding 1: The AI Bottleneck Has Moved From Technology To Deployment
Organizations now have access to frontier models, agent frameworks, workflow orchestration platforms, and low-code environments. The problem is not a lack of tools, but an abundance of tools with no coherent operating model.
Finding 2: AI Is Primarily A Change Management Problem
Successful AI deployments depend more heavily on organizational adaptation than technical capability. Workflow redesign, governance, and user adoption are critical.
Finding 3: Enterprise Software Is Transitioning From Products To Workflows
AI fundamentally changes the economics of enterprise software creation. Value increasingly resides in workflows rather than applications.
Finding 4: Private Equity Has An Emerging AI Multiple Problem
Private equity firms increasingly expect AI investments to drive EBITDA expansion and multiple expansion, but lack standardized frameworks for measuring realized AI value.
Finding 5: The Winners Will Build AI Operating Systems, Not AI Projects
The companies generating meaningful AI value treat AI as an operating model transformation rather than a technology initiative.

Andrew 
My $.02 is that it’s extremely hard to build AI that’s 1-size fits all, because everyone’s data and everyone’s business is so different. And actually replacing labor is a much more complicated process (involving deep integrations and operational change). That’s why no “ai models for X” has succeeded. And why every restaurant that’s had breakthrough tech (see Chipotle App, Domino’s, Starbucks, McDonals) has constructed their own tech rather than using an off the shelf vendor.

For better or for worse - if you want this stuff to REALLY work it can’t just be something you slap on top. We’re also very supporting of vendors, and eagerly use them when that’s the thing that makes sense. It’s just that “buy and implement x” is rarely equivalent to a viable ai strategy.

We c an:
1 - identify the top opportunities for efficiency gains across their business as a result of AI 
2 - drive those improvements through a combination of vendors, custom tools, and operational change
3 - build predictive models that actually fit their restaurants.

Metin Hacioglu
Role: Deputy CEO & COO at FreshDirect
Background: Metin has been with the FreshDirect/Getir ecosystem for nearly 18 years. He served as VP of Global Functions (Operations Development & Indirect Procurement) at Getir, then as Transition Leader overseeing the FreshDirect/Getir integration, before becoming COO of FreshDirect under Getir ownership. In January 2025, he was elevated to Deputy CEO alongside his COO responsibilities. He is based in New York and is the public face of FreshDirect's operational transformation — he was quoted in the Uber Eats partnership announcement (March 2025) and the opening of FreshDirect's first physical retail store in Southampton (June 2025).
Company: FreshDirect is a leading online grocer serving the greater NYC tri-state area, founded in 2002 and headquartered in the Bronx. Revenue is approximately $650M; ~500–600 employees (LinkedIn figure) up to ~3,000 per broader estimates. Owned by a holding company controlled by Getir's co-founders following a 2024 restructuring. In June 2026, FreshDirect secured a $100M commercial mortgage loan from UBS, with proceeds explicitly earmarked for technology modernization and AI-powered capabilities — demand forecasting, supply chain optimization, fulfillment efficiency, and customer experience. The company also expanded to its first physical retail location (Hamptons) and partnered with Uber Eats for same-day on-demand delivery.

- More historical data on events, names, hours, and calendars across as many parks as possible. First iteration of the model performs less accurately on special events - and having more granular data here would be helpful.
- Ticket sales information keyed by purchase vs visit date. Likely the biggest missing forward demand signal. Current ticket data is 2026+ only, so we haven’t been able to backtest on this.
